translation: For all pairs (x,y) of natural numbers with both x and y sufficiently large (eventually in the product filter atTop × atTop), π(x+y) ≤ π(x) + π(y), where π is the prime-counting function.
For all types P and L, with a membership relation of P in L, P finite and L finite, and every projective plane structure pp on (P, L), the order of pp is a prime power.
There exists a rational number t such that: if t > 1, then the real number ∑_{n ∈ ℕ+} 1/(t^n − 1) is irrational.
It is not the case that: for every natural p that is a prime power, and every family H of subsets of Fin(p^2+p+1) that is a pairwise balanced design, if p^2+p+1 < |H|, then p^2+p+1+p ≤ |H|.

There exists a function o: ℕ → ℝ with o(n) = o(1) as n → ∞ (little-o of the constant function 1 at atTop) such that for all sufficiently large n, sumRep(Powerful, n) ≤ n^{o(n)}, where sumRep(Powerful, n) is the number of representations of n as a sum of elements of the set of powerful numbers (as defined by sumRep).

There do not exist real numbers c > 0 and C such that for all natural n ≥ 1, the graph Ramsey number R(C_4, K_n) (with C_4 the 4-cycle and K_n the complete graph on n vertices), as a real number, is ≤ C · n^{2−c}.

For every sequence n: ℕ → ℕ and every rational c > 1: if n is strictly increasing and for all k, c ≤ n(k+1)/n(k) (as rationals), then the real number ∑_{k} 1/F_{n(k)} is irrational, where F_m is the m-th Fibonacci number.

It is not the case that: for every real ε > 0, for all sufficiently large n, every subgraph H of the n-dimensional hypercube graph (on vertex set Fin n → Bool) with |E(H)| ≥ (1/2 + ε) · n · 2^{n−1} contains the 4-cycle C_4 as a subgraph.

For every natural g > 2, for all sufficiently large n: if n ≡ 1 (mod 6) or n ≡ 3 (mod 6), then there exists a family H of subsets of Fin n which is a block design with parameters (2, 3) (i.e. a Steiner triple system: every pair lies in exactly one 3-element block) such that every subfamily E ⊆ H with 2 ≤ |E| ≤ g satisfies |E| + 3 ≤ |⋃_{e ∈ E} e|.
For every natural n > 2, there exist natural numbers x, y, z with 1 ≤ x < y < z and 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z (in ℚ).

It is not the case that: for every n ≥ 3, every finite type V and every simple graph G on V (with decidable adjacency), if the number of edges of G equals C(2n+1, 2) − C(n, 2) − 1 (natural-number subtraction), then there exist simple graphs B, D on V such that (given decidable adjacency instances for B and D) G = B ⊔ D (edge union), B is bipartite, and every vertex v has degree in D strictly less than n.

It is not the case that: for every r ≥ 3, the function n ↦ log^{∘(r−1)}(hypergraphRamsey r n) (the logarithm iterated r−1 times applied to the r-uniform hypergraph Ramsey number) is Θ(n) as n → ∞ (atTop).

There exists f: ℕ → ℝ with f(n) → ∞ as n → ∞, and there exists a natural number n such that every finite set A ⊆ ℝ² with |A| = n that is isosceles-free satisfies f(n) · n ≤ (number of distinct distances determined by A).

There exists a lacunary sequence A: ℕ → ℕ and real numbers u < v such that every rational q with q ∈ (u, v) (open interval) equals ∑_{a ∈ A'} 1/a (computed in ℚ) for some finite set A' ⊆ ℕ contained in the range of A.

It is not the case that: for every k ≥ 3 and every strict total order r on ℝ, there exists a list s of reals which is an arithmetic progression of length k and such that either s is pairwise r-related (each earlier element r-precedes each later one) or s is pairwise related by the flipped relation flip r.

There exists f: ℂ → ℂ that is transcendental over the polynomial ring ℂ[X] and complex-differentiable everywhere (entire), such that for every strictly increasing sequence n: ℕ → ℕ, the set {z ∈ ℂ : there exists k with f^{(n(k))}(z) = 0} is dense in ℂ.
There exists a natural k ≥ 2 such that the set of natural numbers n with ((n+k)!)^2 dividing (2n)! is infinite.

For every rational q > 0 whose denominator is squarefree, there exist a natural k and a strictly increasing function n: Fin(k+1) → ℕ with n(0) = 1 such that for every i in [1, k] (i from 1 to the last index k), ω(n(i)) = 2 and Ω(n(i)) = 2, and q = ∑_{i=1}^{k} 1/n(i) (in ℚ).

For every real c, there exists a natural number n such that either σ(n) > c · n (σ the sum-of-divisors function σ_1), or for every strict covering system m of ℤ there exists an index i such that n (as an integer) does not belong to the modulus ideal m.moduli(i).

The set of triples I: Fin 3 → ℕ+ × ℕ+ such that for every j, (I j).1 ≤ (I j).2 and there exists a positive integer n with ∑_{j ∈ Fin 2} ∑_{m ∈ [(I j).1, (I j).2]} 1/m = n (in ℚ; the inner sum uses only the first two intervals, with the bound variable j re-bound over Fin 2) is finite.

The probability that the binomial random graph on vertex set Fin d → Bool with edge probability 1/2 contains the d-dimensional hypercube graph as a subgraph tends to 1 as d → atBot (the bottom filter on ℕ).
It is not the case that: for every A ⊆ ℕ with natural density 0, for every B ⊆ ℕ, both A ⊆ B + B and |B ∩ [1, N]| = o(√N) as N → ∞.
There do not exist a set A ⊆ ℕ and a real c ≠ 0 such that sumRep(A, n)/log n → c as n → ∞, where sumRep(A, n) is the number of representations of n as a sum of elements of A (as defined by sumRep).
For a natural d, the interior (in ℝ^d) of the set of x ∈ ℝ^d such that for every A ⊆ ℕ, A is infinite, ∑_{n ∈ A} 1/n is summable, and x_i = ∑_{n ∈ A} 1/(n+i) for every i ∈ Fin d, is nonempty.
There exists c > 0 such that for every n ≥ 1, there exists δ: Fin n → ℚ with all values in {−1, 0, 1} such that, letting L = |∑_{k=0}^{n−1} δ_k/(k+1)| (a real number), 0 < L and L < c/2^n.
The function n ↦ Hypergraph.configurationExtremalNumber n 3 6 3 (as a real) is o(n^2) as n → ∞.

Let r ≥ 2 and m ≥ 1 be natural numbers, and G a simple graph on a finite vertex set V with |V| = r·m and minimum degree ≥ m(r−1). Then there exist vertex sets K_1, ..., K_m (indexed by Fin m) such that each K_i is an r-clique in G and the K_i are pairwise disjoint.
For every k ≥ 2, for all sufficiently large n, there exists m with n ≤ m < n + ∏_{i=0}^{k−1} p_i (where p_i is the i-th prime, 0-indexed, so p_0 = 2) such that ω(m) > k.

There exist sets A, B ⊆ ℕ that are complements of each other, such that there is a bijection f: ℕ ≃ A for which the sequence i ↦ f(i) has no monotone arithmetic progression of length 3 (¬HasMonotoneAP ... 3), and there is a bijection g: ℕ ≃ B for which the sequence i ↦ g(i) has no monotone arithmetic progression of length 3.

For every f: ℕ → ℝ: if f(ab) = f(a) + f(b) for all a > 0, b > 0 with gcd(a,b) = 1, and the set {n : n ≥ 1 and f(n+1) ≤ f(n)} has natural density 0, then there exists a real c such that f(n) = c · log n for all n > 0.

There exists real c > 0 such that for every real K > 1 there exists N₀ ∈ ℕ such that for all n and all a: Fin n → ℕ, if n ≥ N₀ and ∑_i 1/a_i > K (in ℝ), then there exists S ⊆ Fin n with 1 − e^{−cK} < ∑_{i∈S} 1/a_i and ∑_{i∈S} 1/a_i ≤ 1.

Let S: ℕ → Set ℂ be such that for every k the derived set (set of accumulation points) of S_k is empty. Then (with the algebra structure Polynomial.algebraPi on ℂ → ℂ) there exist f: ℂ → ℂ and n: ℕ → ℕ such that f is entire, f is transcendental over ℂ[X], and for every k, n(k) > 0 and f^{(n(k))}(z) = 0 for every z ∈ S_k.
For every integer k ≠ 1, the set of natural numbers n with 2^n ≡ k (mod n) (as integers) is infinite.

Let a: ℕ → ℕ be strictly increasing, with a(n)/a(n−1)^2 → 1 as n → ∞ (in ℝ, n−1 natural subtraction), and with the sequence 1/a(n) (in ℚ) summable. Then for infinitely many n (frequently at atTop), a(n) = a(n−1)^2 − a(n−1) + 1 (natural-number arithmetic).
There exists a strict covering system c of ℤ, an index i, and a prime p ≥ 5 such that the modulus ideal c.moduli(i) equals the ideal generated by p − 1, i.e. (p−1)ℤ.

For every strictly increasing n: ℕ → ℕ: if k ↦ 2^{ℵ_{n(k)}} is strictly increasing (as cardinals in universe u) and ℵ_ω < 2^{ℵ_{n(0)}}, then the cardinal partition relation cardinalPartitionRel(∑_k 2^{ℵ_{n(k)}}, 2, 2, (all colors ↦ ℵ_ω)) holds, i.e. κ → (ℵ_ω)^2_2 for κ the cardinal sum ∑_k 2^{ℵ_{n(k)}}.

For all sequences n: ℕ → ℕ and a: ℕ → ℤ, if n(i) > 0 for all i and n is strictly increasing, then there exists d such that the set {x ∈ ℕ : for every i, x < n(i) or x ≢ a(i) (mod n(i))} has logarithmic density d.
Let j ≤ k be natural numbers. If OrdinalMultiColorRamsey(ω_1^3, ω_1·ω, 3, k) holds, then OrdinalMultiColorRamsey(ω_1^2, ω_1·ω, 3, j) holds.
There exists real C > 0 such that every A ⊆ ℕ satisfying, for all sufficiently large N, C·√N ≤ A.countUpTo(N) (the number of elements of A up to N) is subcomplete.
Let P, Q be finite sets of natural numbers consisting of primes, such that 1 = (∑_{p∈P} 1/p) · (∑_{q∈Q} 1/q) in ℚ. Then |P ∪ Q| > 60.
For every A ⊆ ℕ: |{a ∈ A : a ≤ N}| ≪ N/log N (as functions of N), and for all sufficiently large N there exist k and a with k ≥ 0, a ∈ A, and N = 2^k + a.
For every natural d ≥ 3, there exists o: ℕ → ℝ such that either o = o(1) as n → ∞, or for all sufficiently large n, minimalDistinctDistances(ℝ^d, n) = n^{2/d − o(n)}.
For every real C > 0, with f(k, l) = 2^k · 3^l on ℕ × ℕ, the set {∑_{x∈B} f(x) : B a nonempty finite subset of ℕ × ℕ with max_{x∈B} f(x) ≤ C · min_{x∈B} f(x)} has natural density 0.
There exist natural numbers m, n, k such that: if k > 0, then (if m ≥ n + k then lcmInterval(m, k) ≠ lcmInterval(n, k)).
Let α be a real number with α > 0 and α not an integer. Then the set {n ∈ ℕ : n > 1 and gcd(n, ⌊n^α⌋) = 1} (⌊·⌋ the natural floor) has natural density 6/π².

It is not the case that the set of natural numbers r for which there are at least 2 integers m with p_r < m < p_{r+1} whose largest prime factor is < p_{r+1} − p_r is infinite, where p_r denotes the r-th prime (0-indexed).

For all natural r, k with 1 ≤ r < k, for all sufficiently large n: if C(k−i, r−i) divides C(n−i, r−i) for every i < r, then every family H of subsets of Fin n is a block design with parameters (r, k).
There does not exist an infinite set A ⊆ ℝ² in general position such that the integer-distance graph on A (points adjacent when their distance is an integer) has chromatic number ⊤ (infinite).
For every natural N ≥ 2, every k ≥ 2, every natural n, and every m ≥ n + k, N = ∏_{i=1}^{k} (m+i) / ∏_{i=1}^{k} (n+i) (in ℚ).

There exist a type V and a simple graph G on V such that the chromatic cardinal of G is ℵ_1, |V| = ℵ_1, and for every real ε > 0, for all sufficiently large n, every subgraph H of G with exactly n vertices contains a finite set I ⊆ V(H) that is independent in G with |I| > n^{1−ε}.
For every r ≥ 3, the set of n ∈ ℕ that can be written as the sum of a multiset S of natural numbers with |S| ≤ r and every element of S r-full has natural density 0.
There exists a continuous function f: ℝ≥0 → ℝ such that for every c ∈ ℝ≥0, the set {n ∈ ℕ : primeGap(n)/log n ≤ c} has natural density f(c).
Let n be natural and A a finite subset of ℝ^n such that the set of distances {dist(x,y) : x, y ∈ A, x ≠ y} has exactly 2 elements. Then |A| ≤ C(n+2, 2).
For every A ⊆ ℕ with positive upper density, there exist an infinite B ⊆ A and an integer t such that for all b₁, b₂ ∈ B with b₁ ≠ b₂, there exists a ∈ A with a = b₁ + b₂ + t.
For natural numbers n, i with 1 ≤ i and i ≤ ⌊n/2⌋, there exists a prime p with p > i and p dividing C(n, i).
For every natural N ≥ 1, there exists A ⊆ {1, ..., N} that is a Sidon set with N ≤ |A|^3.
For every real c > 0, there exists a real L such that R(k+1, k)/R(k, k) → L as k → ∞ (R the classical two-color Ramsey number) and L > 1 + c.
There exists S ⊆ ℂ such that for all u, t ∈ ℂ with |u| = 1, there exists exactly one z ∈ ℂ such that z ∈ {u·w + t : w ∈ S} and z = a + b·i for some integers a, b.
There exist natural numbers x ≠ y such that x and y have the same set of prime factors, x+1 and y+1 have the same set of prime factors, and x+2 and y+2 have the same set of prime factors.
For every strictly increasing q: ℕ → ℕ such that every q(i) is prime and q(i+1) mod q(i) = 1 for all i, q(k)^{1/k} → ∞ as k → ∞ (with 1/k a real number).
